papers.title: TREM2 encodes plaque macrophage plasticity to mediate atherosclerosis regression
papers.abstract: Cholesterol lowering therapies stabilize atherosclerotic plaque and reduce ischemic events, but the molecular mechanisms governing plaque remodeling or regression remain poorly defined. The lipid sensor TREM2 is a key modulator of plaque-associated foam cell development and was upregulated by plaque macrophages in atherosclerosis regression. We examined macrophage- or monocyte-specific Trem2 deletion during regression in mice and found that TREM2 expression on plaque macrophages, not newly recruited monocytes, was required for plaque regression. Trem2 deletion impeded necrotic core resolution, leading us to interrogate the efferocytic capacity of TREM2+ cells during lipid lowering. An in vitro model of cholesterol-experienced ex-lipid associated macrophages (Ex-LAMs) demonstrated that prior lipid priming enhanced efferocytic ability after unloading lipids and maintained expression of lysosomal and cytoskeletal remodeling genes. Augmented TREM2 signaling through genetic models or agonist treatment accelerated efferocytic ability in vitro and plaque regression in vivo. Thus, we posit that a TREM2-dependent ExLAM programming drives atherosclerosis resolution and facilitates beneficial plaque remodeling through enhanced efferocytosis. Overall, targeting the TREM2 pathway may be a viable strategy for stabilizing atherosclerotic plaques in patients treated with aggressive cholesterol control.

papers.title: Gene regulatory logic underlying the differentiation of mixed lineages in human thymic epithelial cells
papers.abstract: The thymus enacts central tolerance through thymic (TECs), which present self-antigens to developing T cells self-reactive cells, preventing autoimmunity. Human TECs include populations that express lineage-committed programs corresponding to distinct peripheral tissues, yet how they acquire these programs and whether these TEC subpopulations are genetically related and conserved in mice remain unknown. Using matched single-cell gene-expression and chromatin-accessibility profiling of 126,687 human TECs, we identified 17 TEC subsets defined by their distinct expression profiles of 1,843 cell type restricted-antigens (CRAs) from 48 peripheral cell types. With a new phylogenetic reconstruction method, we show that lineage-committed TECs share a common ancestor, retain a thymus-specific mixed identity through co-expression of multiple CRA signatures, and are specified by coordinated activator and repressor regulons. We also identified a basement-membrane-collagen-rich state (BMC-TECs) with progenitor-like properties. Finally, mouse TECs shared the regulatory strategy but conserved few master transcription-factor drivers. This study mechanistically characterizes human TEC subpopulations and reveals the gene regulatory logic that leads to their distinct diversification and mixed identities in humans and mice.

papers.title: A minimal two-residue C-terminal truncation of AID in adult-onset hyper-IgM syndrome type 2 (HIGM2)
papers.abstract: Activation-induced cytidine deaminase (AID), encoded by AICDA, facilitates class-switch recombination (CSR) and somatic hypermutation (SHM) in activated B cells. Loss of AID function causes hyper-IgM syndrome type 2 (HIGM2). While typically autosomal recessive, three C-terminal truncation variants have been reported to act in autosomal dominant manner. We describe a novel heterozygous AICDA nonsense variant, c.589G>T (p.G197*), that truncates the final two C-terminal residues of AID and results in adult-onset HIGM2. Single-cell sequencing of primary patient B cells revealed a complete block in CSR and a [~]10-fold reduction in SHM. AICDA mRNA expression was balanced between wild-type and variant alleles, yet AID protein abundance was reduced to [~]56% with normal subcellular localization. Remarkably, inducible germinal center (iGB) cultures restored CSR in purified naive patient B cells. CRISPR-Cas9 editing of healthy donor B cells confirmed that the iGB platform can rescue B cells harboring heterozygous, but not homozygous, AICDA variants. These results demonstrate that even a two-amino-acid truncation at the AID C-terminus is sufficient to disrupt its function and cause HIGM2.

papers.title: Caspase-1 and -11 defend against environmental but not host-adapted pathogens in genetically complex mice
papers.abstract: Caspase-1 and -11 are inflammatory caspases that trigger pyroptosis, yet in most infection models they confer only a modest survival benefit. We have proposed that caspase-1 and -11 evolved primarily to defend against ubiquitous environmental microbes that have not been under selective pressure to evade them, whereas host-adapted pathogens have evolved evasion strategies. Testing this idea is complicated because the inbred mouse strains used in most infection studies carry mutations in innate immune genes: i.e., C57BL/6 (B6) mice carry a loss-of-function Nramp1 allele, and 129 mice lack functional caspase-11. Here we generated B6 x 129 F1 hybrid mice, which are gene-sufficient at both Nramp1 and Casp11, and used them to measure the fold change in lethal dose ({triangleup}LD100) caused by caspase-1 and -11 deficiency for four pathogens on the B6, 129, and F1 backgrounds. Caspase-1 and -11 conferred little or no survival benefit against the host-adapted pathogens Listeria monocytogenes and Salmonella Typhimurium on any of the three backgrounds, apart from a modest benefit at the lowest S. Typhimurium inoculum in F1 mice. In contrast, caspase-1 and -11 were required to survive infection with the environmental pathogens Burkholderia thailandensis and Chromobacterium violaceum, where caspase-1 and -11 deficiency lowered the lethal dose by up to six orders of magnitude. The failure of caspase-1 and -11 against host-adapted pathogens therefore persists on a genetically robust hybrid background, supporting the view that a major evolutionary role of caspase-1 and -11 is defense against environmental microbes that have not been selected to evade them.

papers.title: Induced microfold cells are required for the function of pulmonary tertiary lymphoid organs that promote mucosal immunity
papers.abstract: Tertiary lymphoid organs (TLOs) arise in response to infection and inflammation. We show that influenza-induced lung TLOs are comprised of inducible M cell (iM cell)-inducible bronchus-associated lymphoid tissue (iBALT) functional composites. iM cells are necessary for the appropriate architecture of adjacent immune follicles, which contain clonally expanded and sequence-diversified B cells. iM cell ablation results in fewer antigen-specific germinal center B cells, T follicular helper cells, and T helper memory cells, and a decrease in secretory IgA and IgG production accompanied by a loss of viral control. We find that the iM cells arise from epithelial progenitors that respond to a RANKL signal from infiltrating T cells, consistent with a model in which the patchy inflammation typical of pneumonia results in the unpredictable and varying distribution of coupled iM cells and adjacent iBALT. We propose that iM cells could be harnessed to promote infection control and enhance mucosal vaccination.

papers.title: Defining the Functional Consequence of the Human Ocular Microbiome
papers.abstract: The ocular surface is one of the body's most environmentally exposed mucosal barriers, yet it is considered low biomass and harbors orders of magnitude fewer bacteria than microbe-rich sites like the gut. This has cast doubt on whether a functional core ocular microbiome exists at all. Having previously defined a protective gd T cell and IL-17 axis engaged by the murine commensal Corynebacterium mastitidis, we asked whether human-derived bacteria could do the same. Pairing sequencing and culturomics of healthy human conjunctiva from two geographically distinct cohorts, we define a stable core microbiome and identify Corynebacterium bovis as a consistent eye-resident commensal rather than a transient contaminant. In humans, C. bovis elicits a non-pathogenic response marked by IL-17 secretion by {gamma}{delta} T cells and circulating C. bovis-specific IgG, which suggests commensalism rather than pathology. Colonizing mice with human C. bovis strains from Pittsburgh or Miami reproduced this program and conferred protection against ocular infection with Staphylococcus aureus. Together, these findings identify C. bovis as a human-derived ocular commensal that can drive protective {gamma}{delta} T cell immunity, translating a mechanism previously defined only in mice into human relevance and a rational target against sight-threatening infection.

papers.title: JAK1/2 Inhibition Restores Tissue Integrity by Rewiring Type 1/2 Immunity Toward Targetable IL-17 Responses
papers.abstract: Effective immune responses require coordinated communication between immune and epithelial cells to eliminate pathogens while limiting tissue damage. Disruption of this balance drives chronic inflammation and progressive tissue destruction. The Janus kinase (JAK) pathway coordinates cytokine signaling across these compartments and has emerged as a therapeutic target in inflammatory diseases. However, the consequences of JAK inhibition within a complex inflammatory environment remain incompletely understood. Here, we dissect the molecular, cellular, immunological and phenotypical effects of topical JAK1/2 inhibition in a chronic model of tissue-destructive skin inflammation driven by barrier dysfunction and bacterial superinfection. Single-cell transcriptomics and functional profiling revealed that JAK1/2 blockade selectively suppressed pathogenic CD8 T cells and their IFN-{gamma} production while shifting Th2-polarized CD4 T cells toward a Th17 phenotype, preserving type 3 immunity consisting of IL-17A-producing {gamma}{delta}-T cells and neutrophil responses. This immune rebalancing occurs rapidly and concomitantly with the restoration of epithelial barrier integrity through tight junction reinforcement, followed by recovery of antimicrobial defenses and reduced bacterial burden. Combination of JAK1/2 and IL-17A blockade further improved tissue homeostasis by targeting residual type 3-driven pathology. Thus, JAK1/2 inhibition acts as selective immunomodulator rather than a broad immunosuppressant, targeting pathogenic type 1/2 responses while preserving type-3-associated antimicrobial defense programs. These findings reveal how JAK1/2 inhibition coordinates immune rebalancing with epithelial repair and support its therapeutic potential in chronic type 1/2-driven inflammatory disease, while identifying residual IL-17A-mediated pathology as a target for combination therapy.

papers.title: CD19-CAR T-cell therapy resets the EBV+ autoreactive B cell repertoire in autoimmune disease
papers.abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) reprograms autoreactive B cells into activated antigen-presenting cells that drive pathogenic T- and B-cell responses in autoimmune disease. Using EBV B-cell sequencing (EBV-seq), we profiled EBV+ B cells in patients treated with CD19 chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells (systemic lupus, n=6; idiopathic inflammatory myopathies, n=3; systemic sclerosis, n=3) or rituximab (n=15). CAR T cells, but not rituximab, depleted EBV+ B cells, resetting the repertoire toward a naive state: predominantly IgM+ with minimal somatic hypermutation. Post-rituximab B-cells remained class-switched, hypermutated, and activated. Monoclonal antibodies cloned from EBV+ B cells lost autoreactivity after CAR T cells but not rituximab. Sustained drug-free remission occurred in 8/12 CAR-treated but 0/15 rituximab-treated patients. EBV+ B cells were predominantly Latency III and resisted anti-CD20 and anti-CD19 antibodies, yet were killed by CAR T cells and T-cell engagers. CD19-CAR T-cell therapy resets the autoreactive EBV+ B-cell repertoire, which may underlie sustained drug-free remission.

papers.title: A network of bZIP transcription factors and inhibitors enforces differentially proliferative and cytotoxic states in T cells
papers.abstract: The bZIP family of transcription factors (TFs) plays a central role in regulating T-cell exhaustion. Their complex dimeric interactions obscure the roles of individual members, which genetic knockout or overexpression alone poorly resolve. Here, we use overexpression of full-length bZIP family TFs alongside genetically encoded, protein-based inhibitors to probe the effect of increased or decreased bZIP TF activity on CAR T-cell expansion under exhausting conditions. Enrichment of inhibitors of pro-exhaustion TFs (CREM, NFIL3) illustrated the utility of this approach. The screen enriched full-length TFs of established anti-exhaustion relevance and identified underappreciated bZIP TFs such as BATF2. Detailed comparison of several bZIP TFs and inhibitors revealed distinct effects on proliferation, persistence, and cytotoxicity. We investigated combinations of pro-cytotoxic JUN, pro-proliferative BATF2, and a novel inhibitor (AEL-CREM) of pro-dysfunction CREM. Distinct pairs were more advantageous for maintenance of cytotoxicity or proliferation, revealing relationships between BATF2, JUN-, and CREB1-family bZIPs. Using a combination of epistasis, transcriptome, proteome, and AP-MS interactome analyses of BATF2 and AEL-CREM, we discovered functional overlap in their inhibition of pro-dysfunction CREB1-family activity, potentially driven by unexpected binding of CREB1-family members by overexpressed BATF2. Their function diverged in BATF2's early promotion of pro-proliferation AP-1 activity and later physical and functional interactions with BACH2, contributing to persistence. These findings were mirrored in murine chronic viral infection and syngeneic tumor models, where BATF2 or AEL-CREM overexpression were notably pro-proliferative and anti-exhaustion. Together, these results illuminate new connections and functional roles enabled by bZIP family perturbations, with implications for modulating T-cell state.

papers.title: A synthetic phageome reveals widespread and diverse human antibody responses to bacteriophages
papers.abstract: Bacteriophages colonize humans, yet their recognition by humoral immunity remains unclear. We developed PhageScan, a PhIP- Seq platform comprising 277,051 phage and 49,630 human viral oligopeptides. Profiling sera from 192 healthy donors without prior phage therapy characterized anti-phage response specificity and revealed widespread, strong IgG reactivity to phages, comparable in prevalence and magnitude to that against human viruses. Recognition patterns were however highly individualized. Among phage sequences, 12,576 peptides were significantly enriched in at least two individuals. Strongly immunogenic epitopes preferentially originated from phages infecting pathogenic bacteria, whereas widely shared ''public'' epitopes were enriched among phages of environmental and food-associated bacteria. ImmE, a lactococcal phage endolysin recognized in 59.9% of individuals, showed reduced antibacterial activity in the presence of sera identified as ImmE-reactive by PhageScan, demonstrating functional relevance. These findings establish phage-directed antibodies as a widespread component of human immunity and PhageScan as a scalable platform for defining phage--antibody interactions.

papers.title: Follistatin-like 1 Promotes Neutrophil-mediated Host Defense against Klebsiella pneumoniae
papers.abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae is a leading cause of pneumonia and highly burdensome etiology of antibiotic-resistant infections constituting an urgent public health threat. Follistatin-like 1 (FSTL-1) is implicated in many processes including lung development and homeostasis, tissue remodeling, and inflammation though its role in antibacterial immunity remains poorly defined. We have observed that FSTL-1 is elevated in the lungs of both humans and mice during bacterial pneumonia. Using an inducible Fstl1 knockout mouse model, we demonstrate that FSTL-1 is required for pulmonary bacterial clearance and neutrophil recruitment during K. pneumoniae infection. Recombinant FSTL-1 rescues Fstl1-deficient susceptibility and enhances clearance of K. pneumoniae in wild-type mice. Mechanistically, FSTL-1-mediated protection was lost upon neutrophil depletion and in Cd14-deficient or Nr4a1 deficient mice, components of a lung-specific neutrophil transcriptional program. These findings identify FSTL-1 as a lung-derived factor that licenses neutrophil-mediated antibacterial defense via a novel FSTL-1/CD14/NR4A1-dependent signaling pathway critical for protection against bacterial pneumonia.

papers.title: Ascorbate and TET2 couple balanced hematopoiesis to disease tolerance
papers.abstract: Infections stimulate myelopoiesis but this comes at the cost of reduced production of other lineages. It is unclear if this imbalance is protective or damaging, and if factors that promote balanced hematopoiesis can impact infection pathology. Here we show that the ascorbate-TET axis limits excessive myelopoiesis, promotes balanced hematopoiesis, and is essential for surviving malaria. Hematopoietic-specific ascorbate depletion promoted myelopoiesis. The effects of ascorbate were mediated by TET2/TET3 activity in myeloid progenitors. Combined ascorbate and TET2 depletion markedly skewed hematopoiesis to the myeloid lineage and impaired erythropoiesis. Ascorbate is commonly depleted in infections, but the functional significance of this remains unclear. In the absence of ascorbate and TET2, mice infected with Plasmodium parasites could clear the pathogen, but had exacerbated myeloid and impaired erythroid response, anemia, and tissue damage and they succumbed to infection, indicating compromised disease tolerance. Therefore ascorbate and TET2 promote balanced hematopoiesis to impart tolerance to malaria.

papers.title: Oleic acid suppresses NLRP3 inflammasome activation to prevent dermal macrophage death and limit imiquimod-induced psoriasis
papers.abstract: Psoriasis is associated with altered lipid metabolism, including reduced expression of fatty acid metabolism genes and decreased circulating oleic acid. Here we report that oral oleic acid supplementation normalized serum oleic acid levels and protected from skin thickening and epidermal hyperplasia in a imiquimod mice model of psoriasis. These effects were associated with preserved skin-resident macrophage numbers and reduced expression of key psoriasis-associated inflammatory markers. Mechanistically, imiquimod induces dermal macrophage death via NLRP3/caspase-1 inflammasome activation, while adoptive transfer of dermal macrophages attenuates psoriasiform inflammation. Oleic acid rescued macrophages from imiquimod and nigericin-induced death in vitro by suppressing NF-{kappa}B and NLRP3/caspase-1 signaling, lowering IL-1{beta} and reactive oxygen species production, and restoring mitochondrial homeostasis, independently of TLR7. Together, our results position dermal macrophage survival as a previously unrecognized checkpoint in psoriasiform inflammation, and suggest that restoring lipid metabolic fitness, rather than solely targeting downstream inflammatory mediators, may offer an additional mechanism-based strategy to limit tissue- damaging inflammation.

papers.title: Pathogenicity of autoreactive TH17 cells is modulated by the TRPM7 kinase
papers.abstract: The melastatin-like transient receptor potential channel, TRPM7, is crucial for signaling in leukocytes. It harbors a channel domain, permeable to divalent cations as well as a serine/threonine -kinase, phosphorylating inter alia SMAD2. TRPM7 kinase activity is essential for the differentiation of non-pathogenic T helper 17 (TH17) cells as well as for T cell colonization and alloreactivity in the gut. As pathogenic TH17 (pTH17) cells drive autoimmune diseases, we studied TRPM7 kinase involvement in pTH17 polarization and function as well as in the development of multiple sclerosis (MS), using human T cells and established murine experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) models. Our results reveal an elevated TRPM7 activity in T effector cells derived from the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) of MS patients, in line with higher functional TRPM7 expression on human TH17 cells. Utilizing a mouse line with disrupted kinase activity (Trpm7R/R), we uncovered both impaired differentiation of pathogenic TH17 cells as well as a significantly milder course of TH17-mediated transfer EAE in Trpm7R/R mice compared to Trpm7+/+ controls. In the CNS of Trpm7R/R mice, the number of FOXP3+ T cells (Tregs) was increased, while fewer TH17 cells infiltrated the CNS due to a migration defect of transferred pTH17 cells in the Trpm7R/R hosts and a failure to reactivate in the intestine, due to reduced MHCII signaling. Thus, inactivation of TRPM7 kinase may represent a promising therapeutic strategy targeting both differentiation and reactivation of pTH17 cells while preserving Tregs function and thereby dampening CNS inflammation in MS.

papers.title: Impact of RNA modification and IL-12 boosts on mRNA-LNP vaccine-elicited CD8+ T cell responses
papers.abstract: Development of effective HIV-1 vaccines requires strategies for inducing both CD8+ T cell and neutralizing antibody responses. Nucleoside-modified mRNA-lipid-nanoparticles (LNP) induce more potent antibody responses than unmodified mRNA-LNP vaccines, while unmodified mRNA is typically employed for CD8+ T cell-inducing vaccines. Here, we compared the abilities of differing ratios of unmodified versus modified mRNA expressing a SIV conserved-region CD8+ T cell immunogen co-administered with IL-12-encoding mRNA-LNP during boosting to induce CD8+ T cell and humoral responses in non-human primates, assessing responses in ChAdOx1-primed controls in parallel. Serial priming and boosting with fully-unmodified mRNA elicited higher-magnitude, more CD8-biased T cell responses than fully-modified mRNA, that were durably maintained after the IL-12-encoding mRNA boosts. Inclusion of 30% nucleoside-modified mRNA enhanced antibody titers, suggesting potential benefits to a mixed-composition vaccine.

papers.title: Developmental IL7/IL7R signaling in fetal resident tissue macrophages regulates adaptive responses to liver injury
papers.abstract: Resident tissue macrophages (RTMs) originate from multiple fetal hematopoietic waves and seed organs during the prenatal window where they acquire tissue-specific homeostatic functions. Several growth factors within the fetal niche are required for RTM development, but knowledge of how these signals program tissue-specific RTM survival, identity, and function during the prenatal window is limited. Here, we investigated the functional role of developmental IL7/IL7R signaling on fetal RTM survival and function. IL7 deficiency impaired neonatal RTM establishment, similar to IL7R deficiency, and IL7 was broadly expressed in fetal tissues and co-localized with IL7R+ macrophages. IL7/IL7R signaling regulated cell cycle, apoptotic, and inflammatory transcriptional pathways and activated phospho-AKT signaling in fetal liver myeloid cells. IL7R deletion impaired proliferation of fetal liver monocyte precursors and increased fetal liver macrophage apoptosis. Specific Cre-mediated IL7R deletion in fetal definitive HSC-derived, but not EMP- derived, macrophages caused irrecoverable postnatal loss of IL7R-expressing macrophages in specific tissues, including the liver, demonstrating a specific temporal requirement for IL7R expression during fetal myelopoiesis. Prenatal IL7R blockade subsequently impaired adaptive responses to chronic fibrotic liver injury in adulthood, associated with increased monocyte infiltration and upregulation of pro-inflammatory signaling pathways. These findings redefine IL7 as a developmental myeloid niche factor and demonstrate that IL7/IL7R signaling is co-opted during fetal development to imprint durable RTM programs that shape postnatal tissue immunity and adaptive responses to injury.

papers.title: Evasion of Hepatic ILC1 Immunosurveillance Drives Breast Cancer Liver Metastasis
papers.abstract: Metastasis, the dissemination of cancer cells to distant organs, is an inefficient process1, yet remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality2. The cellular barriers and evasion mechanisms governing organ-specific susceptibility remain incompletely understood3-5, hindering the development of effective anti-metastatic therapies6. Here, we show that liver-resident type 1 innate lymphoid cells (ILC1s) constitute an essential immunosurveillance barrier against breast cancer liver metastasis that can be bypassed through either cancer cell intrinsic or host-dependent mechanisms. In a multi-organ metastatic breast cancer patient cohort, liver metastasis occurred later and was associated with poorer survival than lung metastasis, with elevated body mass index emerging as a clinical risk factor. This metabolic vulnerability was recapitulated in mice, where a high-fat diet induced hepatosteatosis and selectively enhanced breast cancer colonization of the liver. Mechanistically, liver and lung colonization were restrained by ILC1s and circulating natural killer (NK) cells, respectively. Following cancer cell challenge, NK cells expanded and activated, employing lytic granule pathways and the death receptor DR5 for clearance, whereas activated ILC1s selectively required high DR5 expression on cancer cells, supported by AP-2a (TFAP2A) mediated transcriptional activation, for effective immunosurveillance. Heterozygous copy number deletion at TNFRSF10B (encoding DR5) in human tumours reduced DR5 expression and predisposed to liver metastasis. Hepatosteatosis further compromised this barrier by reducing IL-15 expression in macrophages, thereby depleting hepatic ILC1s effects reversible with glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists. Thus, hepatic ILC1s form a critical organ-specific barrier to breast cancer metastasis, vulnerable to both cancer cell-intrinsic DR5 downregulation and host metabolic dysfunction.

papers.title: Development of a multi-organ single-cell atlas of systemic sclerosis reveals shared and tissue-specific pathogenic pathways.
papers.abstract: Objectives: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a multi-organ autoimmune disease for which no broadly effective disease-modifying treatment exists. We developed an integrated multi-organ single-cell atlas of SSc to identify shared and organ specific disease-associated transcriptional programmes and potential therapeutic targets. Methods: We integrated single-cell RNA-sequencing data from skin, lung, synovium, and peripheral blood mononuclear cells (six studies, 401,902 cells, 90 individuals) using Harmony. Pseudobulk differential expression and gene set enrichment analysis were performed at the tissue cell-compartment, cell-type, and subpopulation levels, including independent reclustering of lymphoid, myeloid and fibroblast populations. Results: Disease-associated transcriptional programmes showed marked tissue dependence, even within the same cell lineage, highlighting the importance of organ-specific mechanisms in SSc. Nevertheless, recurrent extracellular matrix (ECM) remodelling programmes were identified in lung, skin and synovium, and interferon signalling programmes in skin, synovium and peripheral blood mononuclear cells, across immune and fibroblast cell populations. Although no subpopulation was exclusive to SSc, a shared myofibroblast subpopulation expressing SFRP2, COL1A1, POSTN, ACTA2, and COMP was identified across lung, skin, and synovium. In addition, perivascular and mitotic fibroblast subpopulations exhibited both profibrotic and inflammatory signatures, including interferon- and IL-2-related signalling programmes. Conclusions: SSc is characterised by two complementary axes: a tissue-dependent cellular programme and a recurrent fibrotic and interferon-associated signature extending across multiple organs and cell populations. These findings are consistent with current organ-based therapeutic approaches while highlighting interferon signalling as a potential multi-organ therapeutic target. The resulting interactive single-cell atlas provides a resource for investigating shared and organ-specific disease mechanisms and guiding future therapeutic research.

papers.title: CD4 T cell surface architecture is associated with response to anti-PD-1 therapy in non-small cell lung cancer
papers.abstract: Anti-PD-1 therapy has substantially improved outcomes for patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but clinical responses remain highly heterogeneous and are difficult to predict. Current immune profiling approaches primarily characterize immune cell composition and protein abundance, whereas the spatial organization of proteins at the cell surface has remained largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate for the first time that cell surface protein organization is associated with clinical response to immune checkpoint inhibition therapy. Using the Proximity Network Assay (PNA), we simultaneously quantified cell frequencies, protein abundance, and protein organization in pretreatment peripheral blood mononuclear cells from 62 patients with advanced NSCLC treated with anti-PD-1 agents. While most cell populations were unchanged between responders and non-responders, pronounced response-associated alterations were identified within the CD4 T-cell compartment. Responders exhibited elevated expression of adhesion-associated proteins, and remodeling of a CD5-containing membrane domain. Increased colocalization within this domain was associated with poor clinical outcome and reduced survival. Machine learning analysis further identified CD4 T cell features as the strongest predictors of treatment response and demonstrated that protein organization provided greater predictive power than protein abundance alone. Together, these findings identify cell surface protein organization as a previously unexplored source of biomarkers and highlight its potential to improve immune profiling and biomarker discovery in cancer immunotherapy.

papers.title: Inflammation reshapes epidermal and leukocyte differentiation resulting in altered glucocorticoid responsiveness
papers.abstract: Glucocorticoids are widely prescribed anti-inflammatory drugs that act on nearly all cell types due to the ubiquitous expression of the glucocorticoid receptor (GR). While the molecular mechanisms of GR activation have been studied extensively, it is less well understood how GR signaling modulates cell type-specific responses during inflammation. Using the unique attributes of the zebrafish, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing to characterize GR-mediated transcriptional regulation under conditions of wounding-induced inflammation. We found specific cell populations that occurred only under inflammatory conditions within epidermal cells, macrophages and neutrophils. The inflammation-specific subset of epidermal cells showed elevated expression of inflammatory markers, and these cells exhibited a reduced transactivation response to dexamethasone. This reduction in GR activation was also observed in the inflammation-specific subset of macrophages, but not in neutrophils, which retained dexamethasone responsiveness. By correlating the dexamethasone responsiveness with transcriptional coregulator expression, we identified candidate regulatory mechanisms underlying differential GR responsiveness across cell types. Taken together, we provided unique mechanistic insights into cell differentiation during a local inflammatory response and cell type-specific glucocorticoid responsiveness in vivo.

papers.title: Influenza H1N1 Imprinting Uncouples Serological and B-Cell Responses in Mice
papers.abstract: Antigenic drift reduces the protective potential of antibodies generated against earlier influenza variants. Unfortunately, a new infection or vaccination often preferentially recalls antibodies targeting previously encountered strains, thereby limiting responses to newly emerged variants. Although this phenomenon, known as immunological imprinting, has been well documented at the serological level, its underlying cellular mechanisms remain poorly understood. To resolve imprinting at both the serological and cellular level, we combined serum antibody profiling with targeted B-cell characterization in mice, including single-cell B-cell receptor (BCR) sequencing of germinal center (GC) B cells following secondary H1N1 challenge and bulk BCR sequencing of bone marrow plasma cells. We found that a primary infection with the 2009 pandemic H1N1 ("swine flu") strain largely prevented the generation of new serum antibodies following secondary exposure to the antigenically distinct H1N1 strain A/Puerto Rico/8/1934 (PR8), whereas the reciprocal infection sequence updated antibody specificities towards the last encountered virus. GC B cells did not mirror serological imprinting and instead generated updated BCR repertoires directed against the heterologous challenge strain. Likewise, BCR diversity in draining lymph node B cells failed to mirror the serological imprinting observed in the antibody response. Together, these findings reveal a striking uncoupling of cellular and serological immune responses during influenza imprinting, highlighting the need to study both compartments to better understand immune memory and guide the development of improved seasonal influenza vaccines across a diverse population.

papers.title: An interferon-like off-switch in invertebrates: Vago4 downregulates Domeless to restrain JAK/STAT signaling
papers.abstract: Whether invertebrates possess a functional interferon (IFN)-like system remains controversial, as canonical IFN ligands and their receptors are absent from invertebrate genomes. Although Vago proteins in Drosophila and shrimp are compelling functional analogs of IFN, direct evidence for a canonical cytokine-receptor axis and, importantly, for how such signaling is restrained to prevent excessive immune activation, has been lacking. Here, we identify Vago4 as a bona fide ligand of Domeless, the canonical type I cytokine receptor upstream of JAK/STAT signaling. Vago4 binds the extracellular CBM1 and CBM2 domains of Domeless, triggering receptor endocytosis followed by lysosomal trafficking and K27-linked ubiquitination-dependent proteasomal degradation. This ligand-induced receptor downregulation serves as a negative feedback mechanism that restrains excessive JAK/STAT activation. During acute Vibrio infection, Vago4 silencing accelerated shrimp mortality, whereas recombinant Vago4 alleviated inflammatory lesions and oxidative stress, enhanced phagocytosis, and improved survival, phenocopying JAK or STAT knockdown. Thus, by downregulating Domeless, Vago4 limits immunopathology and defines an IRF-Vago4-Domeless-JAK/STAT IFN-like axis in invertebrates, offering new insight into the evolution of IFN-mediated immune regulation.

papers.title: Neutralizing vaccination against viral interleukin-6 from a primate rhadinovirus
papers.abstract: Herpesviruses are ancient viruses that devote a significant fraction of their protein-coding potential to interference with host immunity. Diverse herpesviruses encode proteins with similarity to host MHC molecules, interferon regulatory factors, complement regulators, G-protein coupled receptors, chemokines, and cytokines. Certain gammaherpesviruses, including Kaposi sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV) and rhesus rhadinovirus (RRV), encode viral cytokines similar to host IL-6, called viral IL-6 (vIL-6). The potential of vIL-6 to act as a protective vaccine antigen against these rhadinoviruses remains under-explored. We isolated a new RRV strain, which encodes virion surface proteins similar to those of previous isolates and a vIL-6 that is nearly identical. We found that, although unmodified vIL-6 is a poor immunogen eliciting low neutralizing titers, vIL-6-Fc fusion protein elicits high-titer responses after either one or two doses. We detected no adverse effects related to cytokine activity, nor interference with concomitantly administered vaccine against the RRV glycoprotein B. Our results demonstrate an approach for eliciting neutralizing antibodies against a highly conserved viral protein that contributes to rhadinovirus persistence and oncogenesis.

papers.title: Distinct profiles and antibody production by splenic and lymph node antibody-secreting cells in Trypanosoma cruzi infection
papers.abstract: Evidence from bone marrow and intestinal lamina propria studies indicates that antibody-secreting cell (ASC) characteristics are shaped by the local microenvironment; yet whether secondary lymphoid organs harbor distinct ASC populations during infection remains unclear. Here, we investigated plasmablasts (PB) from the spleen and inguinal lymph nodes (LN) in acute Trypanosoma cruzi infection. Although PB from both tissues expressed canonical ASC markers, they displayed distinct transcriptional, phenotypic, and functional profiles. Splenic PB upregulated genes and proteins associated with inflammation, immunomodulation, and B-cell interactions. Activated and naive B cells also exhibited tissue-specific transcriptional programs, suggesting that local cues influence B-cell differentiation. Consistent with these differences, spleens from infected mice contained more T follicular helper cells, whereas LN were enriched in regulatory T cells. High-dimensional flow cytometry identified multiple PB subsets differentially represented between tissues. Functionally, splenic PB secreted higher levels of IgM, IgA, and IgG, including both parasite-specific and autoreactive antibodies. In contrast, LN PB preferentially produced IgG against peptide 72 of the shed acute-phase antigen (SAPA), despite lower overall T. cruzi-specific antibody production. These findings demonstrate that secondary lymphoid organs harbor distinct PB populations adapted to their local microenvironments during acute infection

papers.title: Intrinsic immune receptor triggering mechanism informs rational chimeric receptor design
papers.abstract: The T cell receptor (TCR) couple antigen recognition to T-cell activation and immune homeostasis. As an eight-subunit assembly, TCR activation operates as a highly coordinated, multi-subunit signaling event. However, which subunit serves as the primary trigger upon ligand engagement still remains unresolved. we identify CD3{varepsilon} as a triggering subunit whose intracellular domain (ICD) is released from the plasma membrane during TCR activation. Elevated membrane tension facilitates this transition from a membrane-proximal to a membrane-distal conformation. The released ICD forms condensates through phase separation with free or co-receptor-associated Lck. These condensates recruit additional CD3{varepsilon} ICDs from neighboring TCRs, triggering resting receptors and promoting further recruitment of TCRs and Lck to amplify proximal signaling. The CD3{varepsilon} ICD alone support robust T cell activation independently of its own ITAM. We observe a similar triggering mechanism in several activating receptors in T and nature killer (NK) cell. These findings support a unifying model in which designated subunits initiate multi-subunit immune receptor activation through phase separation with key kinases. Guided by this model, we engineered triggering molecules (TRIG) that lack canonical intracellular signaling modules. These TRIG molecules recruit endogenous immune receptors in a ligand-dependent manner and efficiently activate both T cells and NK cells. This mechanism provides a basis for designing chimeric receptors that activate immune cells through endogenous receptor signaling.

papers.title: Vaccination targeting the novel endogenous tumor-associated antigen Gpr149 induces protective immunity against checkpoint inhibitor-refractory SB28 glioblastoma
papers.abstract: Background: Glioblastoma is a lethal brain tumor notable for its limited spontaneous induction of CD8+ T cell responses. Vaccination may overcome this limitation by generating tumor-specific CD8+ T cells capable of mediating anti-tumor immunity in the brain. However, preclinical vaccine development is constrained by a lack of immunologically stringent glioblastoma models with defined endogenous antigens. We therefore sought to identify endogenous, vaccine-targetable antigens expressed by the immune checkpoint-refractory SB28 syngeneic mouse glioblastoma model and to evaluate their targetability using a heterologous prime-boost regimen with the chimpanzee adenovirus ChAdOx1 and the modified vaccinia Ankara (MVA) viral vector-based vaccines. Methods: RNA sequencing and whole-exome sequencing were used to identify candidate tumor-associated antigens (TAAs) and neoantigens, and tumor-specific expression was validated by RT-qPCR. ChAdOx1 and MVA vectors encoding candidate antigens were generated and evaluated for immunogenicity and anti-tumor efficacy. Antigen-specific CD8+ T cell responses and minimal epitopes were characterized by ex vivo restimulation, MHC-I binding assays, tetramer staining, and tumor cytotoxicity assays. Results: We identified five candidate TAAs (Gpr149, Cdh6, Fbn2, Igf2bp1, and Shox2) but no suitable neoantigen targets in SB28. Vaccination induced CD8+ T cell responses against the candidate TAAs, and immunogenic minimal epitopes were identified for each. Among the candidates, Gpr149 elicited the strongest vaccine-induced CD8+ T cell responses. In mice challenged intracranially with SB28, Gpr149-targeted ChAdOx1/MVA vaccination combined with immune checkpoint blockade significantly prolonged median survival and resulted in long-term survival in 50% of mice, whereas vaccination targeting the other TAAs did not improve survival. CD8+ T cells recognizing the immunodominant Gpr149128-135 epitope (VCYNFYTM) specifically recognized and lysed wild-type SB28 cells, but not Gpr149-knockout SB28 cells, confirming endogenous processing and presentation of the targeted epitope. Conclusions: Gpr149 is an endogenous SB28 tumor antigen that can be effectively targeted by ChAdOx1/MVA vaccination to generate protective anti-tumor immunity against intracranial glioblastoma. Protection was associated with a dominant CD8+ T cell response to the Gpr149128-135 epitope VCYNFYTM. These findings establish endogenously expressed Gpr149 in SB28 as a physiologically relevant model for evaluating antigen-targeted immunotherapies and provide a systematic approach for identifying endogenous vaccine targets in other preclinical models.

papers.title: Dengue Virus Serotype 2 Infection Transcriptionally Reprograms Host Neutrophils to Establish an Immunosuppressive Microenvironment in Mice
papers.abstract: Dengue virus (DV) infection triggers profound alterations in host immune responses, yet the transcriptomic reprogramming of innate immune cells during disease progression remains incompletely understood. Here, we demonstrated that Dengue virus serotype 2 (DV-2) infection transcriptionally reprograms host neutrophils, establishing an immunosuppressive microenvironment that facilitates pathogenesis. Through scRNA transcriptomic profiling of bone marrow and spleen cells from the DV-2-infected AG129 mouse model, we delineated a distinct neutrophil signature that shows dynamic shifts in immature and activated populations over the course of dengue infection. We also characterized a specific Ly6Glow subpopulation, notably Fibrinogen-like protein 2 (FGL2)-expressing subsets, that appeared with disease progression. Serum FGL2 levels were significantly elevated in both DV-2-infected mice and human dengue-positive patients. Furthermore, treatment of splenocytes with FGL2 or FGL2-enriched neutrophil secretomes suppressed T cell functional activity and promoted an immunosuppressive phenotype. Together, these findings reveal how DV-2-driven neutrophil reprogramming shapes an immunosuppressive network, highlighting the importance of studying FGL2-expressing neutrophil subsets to understand dengue immunopathogenesis.

papers.title: A Synthetic Consensus Chiroptera IFN-β Induces IFN-I Signaling Across Diverse Bat Taxa
papers.abstract: Bat-associated viruses consistently spill over from bats into humans and other animals. Many bat-associated viruses, including Marburg virus and Nipah virus, cause severe disease in humans but their presentation is subclinical in bats. Advancements in tools and resources to study bat innate antiviral immune responses, including the type I IFN (IFN-I) pathway, are needed to evaluate the mechanisms that underlie differential infection outcomes between reservoir bats and spillover hosts. Commercially available IFN-Is are not bat-specific, and conspecific IFN-Is are impractical to produce for the over 1,500 described bat species. Here, we design and validate a bat order-level consensus IFN (Chiroptera IFN-{beta}) that is functional in bat cells from six diverse bat families, including representatives from both suborders. Using Jamaican fruit bat cells, we demonstrate that Chiroptera IFN-{beta} induces an IFN-stimulated gene repertoire comparable to conspecific IFN-{beta}. This valuable resource can accelerate the capacity of the field to study bat innate antiviral responses and illuminate differences between bats and humans.

papers.title: Structures of MyD88 and its oncogenic mutant reveal DNA binding with implications for cytosolic DNA sensing
papers.abstract: MyD88 is a universal adaptor that connects to Toll-like receptors and interleukin-1 receptors through its Toll/IL-1R homology (TIR) domain and activates inflammatory signaling via its death domain (DD). However, how MyD88TIR serves as the platform for these functions and if it has additional functions remain unclear. Here, we report cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of MyD88TIR and its cancer-specific mutant L252P (previously L265P) mainly in ring and spiral forms, respectively. Both assemblies are formed by antiparallel double-filaments, using canonical TIR interfaces within each strand but unique surfaces between the strands, and position MyD88DD at the same sides of the assemblies for self-oligomerization and pathway activation. Surprisingly, these WT or L252P filaments are bound to dsDNA using the concave sides of the rings and the spirals. In vitro assays and cellular studies establish that MyD88 directly binds dsDNA and promotes inflammatory cytokine expression, particularly pro-IL-1{beta}, following dsDNA transfection or viral infection. Notably, these responses are unaffected by deficiency of UNC93B1, the essential chaperone required for trafficking endosomal nucleic acid-sensing TLRs. Structure-guide MyD88 mutant that disrupts dsDNA binding specifically compromises dsDNA-induced transcriptional program while maintaining TLR signaling. RNA-seq further reveals that MyD88 plays a crucial role in inducing gene expression upon dsDNA sensing and that about half of cGAS-dependent genes are also MyD88-dependent. Together, our structural, biochemical and genetic data support the findings that MyD88 directly engages with cytosolic dsDNA and cooperates with cGAS to promote the full innate immune transcriptional response.

papers.title: Vaccination of pregnant mares with mRNA encoding a GPI-anchored form of the virulence-associated protein A of Rhodococcus equi induces strong IgG responses that are transferred to their foals
papers.abstract: The bacterium Rhodococcus equi is a common cause of severe pneumonia in foals worldwide. Foals are exposed to R. equi from birth and are most susceptible in the first weeks of life. In North America, control measures are limited to transfusion to newborn foals of hyperimmune plasma whose potency is assessed by surpassing a threshold of IgG against the virulence-associated protein A (VapA) of R. equi. Here we report results of vaccination of pregnant mares with mRNA encoding a GPI-anchored virulence-associated protein A (VapA) of R. equi induced VapA-specific IgG subisotypes transferred to their foals during the 63-day period after birth. Pregnant mares were randomly assigned to receive either VapA mRNA vaccine (n=10) at 8 and 10 months of gestation or no vaccine (n=10). Serum was collected from mares at 8 months of gestation (before vaccination for immunized mares) and {approx}24 hours after foaling and from foals at ages 1, 35, and 63 days. Mean relative concentrations of were low before immunization in all mares and did not change over time in unvaccinated mares; however, mean relative concentrations of anti-VapA IgG1, IgG4/7, and IgG3/5 of mares were significantly increased after VapA mRNA immunization and strongly correlated with the corresponding concentrations in their foals sera at age {approx}24 hours. Concentrations of anti-VapA IgGs remained increased in foals of vaccinated mares compared with control foals for at least 35 days.
